C0.quote: nodes as voters and outgoing edges as their support for other nodes
C0.note: Committee selection rules from network votes (MES-based election rules and absorbing rules); axiomatic, complexity and experimental analysis.

C1.quote: We analyze our methods axiomatically and characterize their behavior on special graph classes
C1.note: Axioms (Thm 4,5, Prop 3), NP-hardness and poly-time (Thm 1,2), experiments on real and synthetic data. Axiomatic is the largest share, roughly.

C2.1.value: graph/network; edges as votes; election profile (V, C, µ)
C2.1.quote: outgoing edges as their support for other nodes, or simply their votes

C2.2.quote: We consider unweighted simple directed graphs.
C2.2.note: Input is a directed graph (edges as votes/approvals). Then transformed into utilities µ (CARD) for MES, but the rule's input is the graph.

C2.3.note: Edges are votes; utilities µ are derived from the graph by the method, not held attitudes. Euclidean positions are only for generating graphs.

C2.4.quote: outgoing edges as their support for other nodes, or simply their votes
C2.4.note: Input only described as submitted votes.

C4.1.note: Input is a graph (OTH); utility µ is derived from graph, not from RANK/APPR etc.

C5.1.quote: a cohesive group S is entitled to ⌊k · |S |/n⌋ representatives
C5.1.note: Proportional representation axioms and experiments measuring proportionality of outcomes.

C5.2.quote: each node should have a significant influence over k/n of the committee
C5.2.note: Evaluated on the graph (the input) without any statement relating to held attitudes.

VOT.note: Nodes' edges are fixed inputs; no voter actions modelled as choices.

ORG.note: The rule selects; no organiser choice modelled.

claims.quote: our approach combines the benefits of indirect democracy with a more personalized voting process
it is also a prefarable method to be combined with centrality measures
performs best across the datasets used in our evaluation

C9.1.note: Claims on institutions and which rule to prefer.

C9.2.quote: fostering a stronger connection between voters and their representatives
C9.2.note: Claims about representation of voters/democracy need an assumption that edges reflect voters' actual support and that voters vote sincerely; not stated.

C10.1.note: No statement of a procedural reading.
